title: Gradient Boosting
objectives: Explain the key ideas behind Gradient Boosting.
Describe why Gradient Boosting matters in Data Science.
Apply Gradient Boosting to a realistic scenario.
Identify common pitfalls and how to avoid them.
Answer interview questions about Gradient Boosting.
definition: Gradient Boosting is a core concept in Data Science. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What Gradient Boosting is
theory.body: Gradient Boosting describes the methods and patterns used within Data Science to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: Gradient Boosting is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why Gradient Boosting matters
theory.body: Without Gradient Boosting, systems built with Data Science are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How Gradient Boosting works
theory.body: The mechanism behind Gradient Boosting follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of Gradient Boosting.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of Gradient Boosting
theory.body: Gradient Boosting offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
